cost_note: Published per-image rate for one Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image 1K output. The Gemini Developer API generateContent response carries no per-call invoiced dollar amount, so measured spend is (successful images x published per-image rate) — the same basis every prior Gemini receipt in this repo uses. Token usage per call is recorded in usage_metadata as corroborating evidence. A blocked/safety-filtered image is not charged (confirmed by the provider's own error message) and is excluded from total_cost_usd.

Intended use: a background plate for a marketing asset. Large display type is set over it afterwards in Photoshop, so this image is the surface, not the finished piece. Set polish accordingly: real, worn and restrained, not advertising-slick.
Scene / background: A narrow commercial street at first light, overcast. A corrugated steel roller shutter pulled fully down across a small storefront, filling the frame edge to edge, its slats dented and re-painted grey many times over.
Subject: The lower half: the base of the shutter meeting a cracked concrete sidewalk, with a loading-bay floor marking painted on the concrete directly in front of it in chalky yellow. That marking is PURE GEOMETRY ONLY - one plain unbroken rectangle outline and one solid painted bar inside it, nothing else - and contains absolutely no letterforms, numerals, characters, glyphs, arrows, symbols or anything that could be mistaken for writing. Half of it is scuffed away by foot traffic.
Key details: Rust bleeding at the shutter's bottom rail, a padlock hasp, scraped paint layers, grit and a flattened bottle cap in the concrete seam, tape residue where a sign was once fixed and removed.
Camera and light: 35mm, straight on, eye level, flat overcast light with one hard raking edge from the left, deep focus so the shutter face reads as a texture across the whole upper frame.
Photograph it, do not illustrate it: real optics, natural depth of field, one dominant light source, coarse visible film grain, and honest material wear - scuffs, dents, dust, chalky faded paint, rust bloom, tape residue, torn paper edges, uneven weathered surfaces. Hard directional light and deep shadow; high contrast, crushed blacks, a slightly overcooked photocopy quality as if the frame were xeroxed once and screen-printed once. Ordinary and unstaged, as if caught in the moment on a working day. Do not render it as 8K, ultra-detailed, hyper-real, studio-polished, cinematic, or heavily retouched.
Colour world (mandatory): cold rolled steel and grey concrete, #16181A - a dark neutral grey with a faint blue-green cast - filling most of the frame. Exactly ONE saturated accent anywhere in the image: a weathered, chalky stencil yellow, #E4C227, and it is always PAINTED PIGMENT ON A SURFACE - loading-bay floor paint, a curb marking, a shutter warning stripe, hand-lettered signboard paint - never a light source, never a glow, never a lamp. Every other surface is neutral, cold and desaturated: bare concrete, galvanised metal, dirty white, grey primer, with rust brown only at worn edges. No blue sky, no green, no neon, no warm interior lamp, no second saturated colour anywhere.
Reserved negative space (mandatory): the top 50% of the frame stays near-empty - one continuous low-detail surface (a wall, a shutter face, an overcast sky, a seamless ground) carrying no subject, prop or high-contrast texture. Weight the subject into the lower half. That empty band is where display type lands in Photoshop. The emptiness must be REAL DEPTH IN THE SCENE - an actual wall, sky or surface receding naturally with its own soft light gradient, grain and imperfection. It is NOT a blank panel, card, sheet, sticker, overlay, crop or flat rectangle placed on top of the photograph. Never introduce a hard straight edge, a colour block or a uniform fill to create it. If the scene cannot provide that emptiness honestly, re-frame the shot until it can.
Text rule (absolute): render zero text. No letters, numerals, words, handwriting, printed copy, signage lettering, screen copy, UI labels, packaging copy, captions, watermarks, signatures, logos or brand marks anywhere in the frame - including on paper, screens, clothing, vehicles, tools and boxes. Where the scene would normally carry writing, show that surface blank: blank cards, blank paper, blank sign panels, dark or face-down phones, unlabelled folders. All type is set in Photoshop afterwards; a plate that arrives with generated lettering is unusable.
Exclude: any person, face, hand, body part or silhouette; a second saturated colour, rainbow gradients, neon signage, lens-flare stars, HDR halos, teal-and-orange grading, blown highlights, low-contrast haze, obvious stock-photo posing, real identifiable people or celebrities, 3D-render or CGI look, vector or illustration look, dutch tilt, heavy motion blur, collage, borders, frames, device mockup edges, graffiti tags or street-art murals, and any object not named above.
Preserve on every revision: the colour world, the reserved empty area, the framing and lens, the single dominant light source, the coarse grain, and the complete absence of text and people. Change only what a revision explicitly asks to change; do not alter anything else.
